content.title: Chevrolet Confirms Corvette Grand Sport Pricing, and ZR1X Gets a Huge Price Hike
content.text: Chevrolet has confirmed pricing for the 2027 Corvette lineup, including the Grand Sport and Grand Sport X, which were revealed earlier this year. The Stingray starts at $73,495, the Grand Sport at $88,495, the Grand Sport X at $112,195, the Z06 at $121,395, the ZR1 at $197,195, and the ZR1X at $227,395. Chevrolet dealerships will start taking orders for most of the Corvette lineup on April 16, with Grand Sport X order books opening this summer. As the vernal season marches on, trees are beginning to bud, flowers are starting to bloom, and car owners everywhere are preparing their vehicles for the first car shows of the spring season. Oddly enough, the Corvette bush we planted out back in the fall is starting to show new life as well—and Chevrolet just confirmed pricing for the 2027 lineup to Car and Driver. Pricing for the full range of 2027 Vettes first appeared on a Corvette Forum, which a Chevrolet spokesperson later confirmed as accurate to C/D. The big news is the announcement of the prices for the Grand Sport and Grand Sport X. The former carries a starting price of $88,495, and the latter is priced at $112,195. Adding the Track Performance package to the Grand Sport moves the needle to $109,190, while switching to the hardtop convertible of either GS adds $7000 to the base price. There's also a non-track performance pack for the Grand Sport that costs $3500 and includes Michelin Pilot Sport 4S tires and performance brakes from the Z06. Chevy confirmed pricing for the rest of the Corvette lineup as well, and things got considerably more expensive at the top end. The ZR1 now starts at $197,195, which marks an increase of $9700 over the 2026 version. The ZR1X price change is even more significant: it now starts at $227,395, up from $212,195. Thankfully, the Stingray and the Z06 remain the performance bargains that they've always been. The base Stingray now starts at $73,495, up $1000 from last year. The Z06 is up slightly more and starts at $121,395, marking a $1700 jump. Chevrolet dealerships will start taking orders for the bulk of the Corvette lineup as early as April 16. According to Chevy, the Grand Sport X will go on sale sometime this summer. This content is imported from poll.
